title: T1588.001 — Obtain Capabilities - Malware
subtitle: Interactive walkthrough of Obtain Capabilities - Malware with the technique-specific attack path and defender evidence.
aria: Attack simulation, step 1 of 8. Planning the malware shopping list. The attacker lists what the attack needs: a stealer for credentials or a ransomware build for extortion. They compare renting a RaaS product with buying a stealer or taking open-source malware.

steps.defender: Nothing is visible. No packet, file, or account of yours is involved yet.

steps.title: Renting on the RaaS panel
steps.caption: The actor pays in cryptocurrency and receives a login for the malware panel. LAPSUS$ used the bought Redline stealer this way, and TA2541 ran strains bought on criminal forums.
steps.defender: You still see nothing, but vendors track the family. Its hashes and reports will reach threat intelligence.

steps.title: Building and packing the payload
steps.caption: On the panel the actor sets the C2 address and options, then generates the binary and wraps it in a packer so scanners see only an encrypted blob. APT-C-36 used the HeartCrypt and PureCrypter services this way.
steps.defender: A faint signal exists: packer services leave build patterns, and researchers note new builder activity in reports.

steps.title: Staging on fresh infrastructure
steps.caption: The actor uploads the payload to a server behind a freshly registered domain and requests a TLS certificate for it.
steps.defender: First real visibility: certificate transparency logs publish the new certificate within minutes, and passive DNS shows a days-old domain.

steps.title: Testing in a sandbox
steps.caption: The actor runs the sample on a clean virtual machine and checks that the beacon works and the packer holds up. Buyers often test before use.
steps.defender: Test copies leak into sandboxes and repositories. A hash now exists in public databases for intelligence to match later.

steps.title: Delivering the payload to the target
steps.caption: The actor sends phishing mail with a link to the staging server, or hosts a fake installer on a web page. The message is well written and passes.
steps.defender: The mail gateway sees a low-reputation sender with a payload link. One weak signal appears and is usually not enough to alert alone.

detection.label: Partial signal
detection.detail: A weak signal exists but is not yet a confirmed alert.

steps.title: First run and C2 check-in
steps.caption: A user opens the lure. The dropper writes the payload to a user-writable folder and starts it. The implant calls the staging server over HTTPS and waits for orders.
steps.defender: Endpoint and proxy logs now hold a new unsigned process and a connection to a days-old domain. Paired with the certificate alert from step 4, this is a strong signal.

detection.detail: The SOC has enough evidence to open an incident.

steps.title: The SOC joins the dots
steps.caption: Threat intelligence matches the hash, the packer traits, and the domain. The SOC pivots from the mail to the host to the beacon and opens a case.
steps.defender: Each event alone looked weak. Correlation across intelligence and telemetry turns the fragments into a confirmed case: host isolated, credentials reset.
